description: A single-panel figure consisting of one scanning electron micrograph (secondary-electron, plan-view contrast) of the Fe-6.8Al alloy annealed at 750 °C for 60 min, as stated in the caption. A white horizontal scale bar in the lower-right corner is labelled "300 µm"; there are no axes, legends, phase labels or data annotations. The surface shows an equiaxed, polygonal grain structure: grains are outlined by dark, continuous boundary grooves, while grain interiors are mid-grey and largely featureless, indicating a fully recrystallised, strain-free microstructure with no visible elongated/pancaked deformation bands or shear bands. Individual grains span only a small fraction of the 300 µm scale bar, so the grains are tens of micrometres across, but no grain-size value is printed on the image itself (the citing text states the grain/crystallite size is reported in Table 2, not in this figure). A sparse population of dark angular pits and particles, presumably inclusions, pores or etching artefacts, is scattered over the surface, together with a few faint, diffuse brighter patches. The panel, read with the citing text, demonstrates that 60 min at 750 °C converts the 98% cold-rolled Fe-6.8Al structure into equiaxed, fully recrystallised grains that have coarsened relative to the 5 min anneal.

No other annotations are present.

observations.observation: The figure contains exactly one panel: a secondary-electron SEM micrograph with no sub-panel labels, axes, legend or data annotations.
A white horizontal scale bar in the lower-right corner is labelled '300 µm'.
The grains are equiaxed and polygonal, delineated by dark continuous boundary grooves, with largely featureless mid-grey grain interiors.

No elongated/pancaked grains or shear bands are visible, whereas the citing text states the 98% cold-rolled condition shows heavily elongated pancaked grains and shear bands at ~40° to the RD with deformed lamellae 2.6 ± 1.2 µm wide.
Individual grains span only a small fraction of the 300 µm scale bar, i.e. the grain size is on the order of tens of micrometres; no numerical grain size is printed on the image.
Sparse dark angular pits/particles are scattered across the surface, consistent with inclusions, pores or etching artefacts.
The caption states the image is of the Fe-6.8Al sample annealed at 750 °C for 60 min.
The citing text states that the sample annealed for 60 min shows equiaxed and fully recrystallised grains.
The citing text states that grain growth can be observed for the sample annealed for longer times (sentence truncated in the supplied text).
The citing text states the grain/crystallite size is reported in Table 2, so this figure itself carries no grain-size number.
